answers.answer: As of the change in ripgrep PR #2957, you can source them dynamically: `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` [C1]. Previously this failed with a zsh error (`_arguments:comparguments:327: can only be called from completion function`), and the only workaround was writing the script to a file in your fpath [C2][C3]. Note that this generate-and-source approach is slower (~4ms per invocation), which is imperceptible alone but can add up, so it's documented in the FAQ with a caveat emptor [C4][C5]. It may require a self-built ripgrep, since the timing of the next release isn't known [C6].

Only space padding is supported — the decision was to start with spaces and add more padding support later as needed [C6]. This is because Rust's format! macro can't take a custom padding character as a parameter (only the width), so the padding character has to be hard-coded in the format string [C5]; supporting arbitrary padding characters was the originally explored approach but was rejected [C10]. Relatedly, a width starting with zero must return an error [C2].

answers.answer: The tool must return an error if the padding width starts with a zero [C2]. More generally, the width should error if it starts with anything other than 1-9, though that case is already covered in the PR because such input fails to parse as an integer [C3]. One suggested implementation is to check the argument string before converting to usize, store a boolean (arg.starts_with("0")) in the Args struct, pass it to the printer, and use an if condition to pick the format string [C9] — needed because Rust's format! macro cannot accept a custom padding character as a parameter [C5], and the decision was to start with space padding only [C6].
